data.narrative:
Quobly is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Maud Vinet, Tristan Meunier, and François Perruchot. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 identifiable comparables: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The peer-median valuation method is not applicable to Quobly. The quantum computing sector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage seed comparables with reliable valuation data; filtering the 8 private peers by stage and valuation tier yielded fewer than the minimum 3 datapoints required for a defensible median. An all-sector median would obscure material stage and capital-efficiency differences between seed-stage and later-stage quantum ventures, introducing bias rather than clarity.

Without a triangulated range from comparable company analysis, this valuation cannot be anchored to observable market transactions. Proceeding would require alternative methods—such as discounted cash flow analysis (limited by absence of revenue or detailed financial projections for a seed-stage company) or venture capital method inputs (which depend on assumed exit valuation and target IRRs not provided here). The primary constraint is the early stage of the company relative to the depth of public market comparables and the sparseness of seed-stage private transactions in quantum computing. Further data collection on recent seed or Series A quantum company rounds would be necessary to establish a credible valuation range.
